opex.text: The liquidity needs of the Holding Company on an unconsolidated basis consist primarily of operating expenses, interest payments on debt, and shareholder distributions in the form of dividends and stock repurchases. During the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, holding company operating expenses consisted of interest expense of $2.1 million and $1.3 million, respectively, and other operating expenses of $1.8 million and $1.5 million, respectively. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, holding company operating expenses consisted of interest expense of $5.3 million and $4.1 million, respectively, and other operating expenses of $6.4 million and $3.7 million, respectively. Additionally, the Holding Company paid $9.1 million and $6.7 million of dividends to stockholders during the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and paid $24.8 million and $20.0 million of dividends to stockholders during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The following table sets forth the components of provision for credit losses for the periods indicated:

Comparison of the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 to the Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

The Company recorded a negative provision for credit losses of $0.6 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a $0.6 million provision during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The negative provision for credit losses during the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflects a $1.9 million decrease in required reserves driven by changes within the portfolio, which included net recoveries of $0.5 million; a $0.6 million decrease in required reserves driven by changes in the economic forecast; a $0.1 million decrease in specific reserves; and a $2.0 million increase in required reserves resulting from changes in qualitative factors.

Comparison of the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 to the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025

The Company recorded a negative provision for credit losses of $41 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a $1.7 million provision during the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table sets forth the major categories of noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Comparison of the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 to the Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Total noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $42.7 million, an increase of $10.2 million, or 31.2%, from the three months ended September 30, 2025. Notable changes in noninterest expense include the following:

• Acquisition-related expenses of $1.0 million recognized during the third quarter of 2026 were absent during the third quarter of 2025; and

• Excluding acquisition-related expenses, the $9.2 million increase in noninterest expense was primarily attributable to the addition of CNB’s operations, including a $5.8 million increase in salaries and employee benefits, which were also driven higher by annual merit increases and higher medical benefits costs.

Comparison of the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 to the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025

Total noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $137.5 million, an increase of $41.2 million, or 42.7%, from the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income equals the excess of interest income on interest earning assets (including discount accretion on acquired loans plus certain loan fees) over interest expense incurred on interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest margin, which is expressed as the percentage of net interest income to average interest-earning assets, is utilized to measure and explain changes in net interest income.

The following tables set forth average balances, average yields and costs, and certain other information. Average balances are daily average balances. Nonaccrual loans are included in the computation of average balances but have been reflected in the table as loans carrying a zero yield. The yields set forth below include the effect of deferred fees and costs as well as purchase accounting adjustments that are accreted or amortized to interest income or expense.

intro.text: HBT Financial, Inc. (the “Company” or "HBT Financial"), a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1982, is a bank holding company headquartered in Bloomington, Illinois that has elected to be regulated as a financial holding company. As of December 31, 2025, we had total assets of $5.1 billion, loans held for investment of $3.5 billion, and total deposits of $4.4 billion. Through our bank subsidiary, Heartland Bank and Trust Company (“Heartland Bank” or the “Bank”), we provide a comprehensive suite of financial products and services to consumers, businesses, and municipal entities throughout Illinois and eastern Iowa. The Company’s common stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “HBT.”

lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities

accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
